title: Heat Pumps Aren't for Everyone in Toronto & the GTA to Etobicoke—Find Out Why!
summary: Toronto HVAC contractor warns about defrost meltwater on driveways and heat pumps costing more than air conditioners, while promoting their savings.

assertions.quote: there is going to be water that's going to be around the system

verdicts.note: Defrost meltwater drains from the outdoor unit and can refreeze on paved surfaces in sub-freezing weather.

assertions.quote: on some units they can be as high as 3, 4,000 dollars more than an air conditioner.

verdicts.note: Standard heat pumps usually cost modestly more than a same-size AC, while cold-climate variable-speed models cost several thousand more.
Wholesale prices are only $200-$500 more than equivalent ACs, but installed heat pumps sized for heating often cost more because of larger capacity and electrical work.
Edwards' national installed-cost medians at the same 36,000 BTU/h size are $6,185 for a heat pump and $4,684 for a central AC, about 30% apart.
NREL cost database: heat pump $2,994 base / $5,550 efficient versus central AC $3,164 / $5,180; the report says heat pumps cost very similar to split AC of the same SEER.

assertions.quote: Cuz they they do exactly what an air conditioner does.
And they're going to really make a big difference on how much you're paying month over month.

verdicts.note: For gas-heated homes, as most in Ontario are, measured bill savings are small or negative; large savings are mainly for oil, propane or resistance homes.
Minimum-efficiency units save only $100/yr on average and raise bills for 39% of households; high-efficiency units save $740/yr on average but still raise bills for 5%.
Edwards finds 19% of households would pay more and 28% show no clear change with a heat pump, so substantial bill cuts are not general.

LBNL: many electrification projects achieved large energy cost reductions, but some increased costs in high-rate states; savings depend on the fuel replaced and local rates (savings were mostly modeled, not metered).
Every monitored site saved: ducted propane sites cut costs 28-40% ($377-$764/yr) and ductless resistance sites 52-54%; only propane and resistance baselines were tested, not gas.

For UK households coming off gas boilers, running costs went slightly up (about £190/yr, or £83 net of the gas standing charge), not substantially down, against a pre-switch energy bill of about £2,200/yr.

assertions.quote: they've been consistently going up in price every year, year after year after year.

verdicts.note: HVAC equipment prices rose sharply in 2021-2025 with inflation and the refrigerant transition, but future prices and incentives are uncertain.
